parts.note: a letter of reference written by a former boss, with a nod to a single letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone receives a letter from the firm they used to work for.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is both a written symbol (a letter) and an old-fashioned name for the testimonial a former employer writes.
explanation.definitionFit: An employer's testimonial was traditionally called a character, and a letter of the alphabet is also a character.

parts.note: CAs are chartered accountants, so the plural gives CAS
taken as written
wary means cautious

explanation.surface: A bird-watcher observes how careful accountants are.
explanation.walkthrough: CA is the usual abbreviation for a chartered accountant.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flightless bird of Australia and New Guinea.

clue.text: Humble sailor goes on sea trip

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the stock crossword sailor

indicators.note: trip suggests stumbling, so the letters of sea fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A modest sailor sets off on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' looks like a voyage but is the anagram signal for SEA, giving ASE after AB.
explanation.definitionFit: To abase someone is to humble or degrade them.

clue.text: They flew by way of hill, in a certain direction

indicators.note: the words before it are placed inside the following ones

parts.note: S, south, is one particular compass direction
via means by way of
a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: Pilots took a route over a hill heading one way.
explanation.walkthrough: VIA and TOR go inside A and S. TOR is a rocky hilltop, common on Dartmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen are people who fly, so they are the ones who flew.

parts.note: stretcher cases suggests patients carried on stretchers, but the treatment literally stretches injured limbs

explanation.surface: Something used on patients carried by stretcher.
explanation.walkthrough: A stretcher case is a badly injured patient; the treatment meant is one that pulls a broken limb straight with weights.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical traction applies a steady pull to stretch and align a fractured limb.

indicators.note: rebuilding means the letters of are are put together in a fresh order

parts.note: the LMS was the London, Midland and Scottish Railway, a British company before nationalisation

explanation.surface: Areas are reconstructing a disused railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilding' rearranges ARE into REA, then LMS follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Realms are kingdoms or domains, that is regions.

parts.note: read not as gunmen or picketers but as things on the ends of arms that strike

explanation.surface: Workers on strike carry weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Armed' means attached to an arm, and 'strikers' are things that hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Clenched hands are at the end of the arms and are used to punch.

clue.text: Weak part of Henry IV Part 2

definitions.meaning: a role in Shakespeare's play: Francis ..., a recruit Falstaff enlists

explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare gave his rustic recruits telling names; Feeble the woman's tailor is one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Weak means lacking strength, and Feeble is also a role played in Shakespeare's history play.

parts.note: looks like agreeing with the captain, but means the right-hand side of the captain's ship

explanation.surface: Grudging agreement that the skipper might be correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' is the direction, not correctness; the right side of a ship facing forward.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, the right-hand side when facing the bow has its own nautical name.

clue.text: Things we are content to promise

indicators.note: the contents of the words Things we are are the letters held inside them

explanation.surface: We are happy to commit to certain things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like contentment but signals what the words contain.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear is to vow or give one's solemn word.

clue.text: Nat's. aim is to develop staying power

indicators.note: develop suggests the letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: the name Nat with its S
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nat intends to build up his endurance.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'Nat's' counts here; the letters of NATS and AIM are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is endurance, the capacity to keep going.

parts.note: ave is a Latin greeting, hail
rage means storm, as in to rage or storm about

explanation.surface: A typical hailstorm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hail-storm' splits into a greeting and an outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: Average means ordinary or typical.

clue.text: Open bowling before start of Test?:

parts.note: an over is a spell of six balls bowled in cricket

indicators.note: start points to the opening letter of Test

explanation.surface: A bowler opens before a cricket Test match begins.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six deliveries; a Test is an international match.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly, not hidden.

parts.note: William Temple was Archbishop of Canterbury
the Bar is the body of barristers

explanation.surface: An archbishop has a meeting with lawyers in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the old gateway site on Fleet Street, beside the Inns of Court where lawyers work, hence 'in London'.
explanation.definitionFit: The landmark stands in the City of London where Fleet Street meets the Strand.

clue.text: Where people wait in African mountain retreat

indicators.note: retreat means go backwards, so the joined pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: a Moor is a North African
Etna is the Sicilian volcano

explanation.surface: A hideaway on an African peak where travellers wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' looks like a hideaway noun but turns MOORETNA backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A waiting room or lobby outside a main room.

clue.text: For telling to the highly credulous

definitions.text: For telling to the highly credulous

parts.words: For telling to the highly credulous
parts.note: an unlikely yarn that only someone very gullible would swallow, with highly hinting at height

explanation.surface: Something to recount to the gullible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'highly' points to the adjective for height used of an exaggerated tale.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaggerated, unbelievable account is called this, and only the gullible believe it.

parts.note: a mild four-letter oath stands in for a ruder one, and the punctuation mark replaces censored words

explanation.surface: Substituting one short word for another.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'four-letter word' is a swear word; this mild exclamation, and the printed mark, stand in for one.
explanation.definitionFit: The mild oath is a polite substitute for a stronger curse, and a typographical mark replaces a censored word.

indicators.note: a translation turns words into a different form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone reads Smith in a foreign language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective but names a Dickens novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's 1854 novel set in Coketown.

clue.text: Power appears to depend on rise of revolutionary leader

parts.note: the watt is the unit of power

indicators.note: in a down clue rise means the word is read upward

parts.note: rely means depend

explanation.surface: Power seems to rest on a rebel leader rising up.
explanation.walkthrough: RELY read upward gives YLER. The rebel led the Peasants' Revolt of 1381 in England.
explanation.definitionFit: He led the English Peasants' Revolt, a revolutionary uprising.

parts.note: a payment that keeps a lawyer engaged, with keeper hinting also at a servant kept on

explanation.surface: What a goalkeeper or warden is paid.
explanation.walkthrough: The payment is to keep someone's services; the word also means an old servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A fee paid in advance to secure a barrister's services; the word also names a long-serving servant.

indicators.note: backs means the joined pieces are written backwards

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
ay is an old word for yes

explanation.surface: A college supports the Spanish accord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' looks like 'supports' but turns ELAY round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ivy League university in New Haven, Connecticut.

clue.text: Tip to put in a washer in the plant

indicators.note: put in means the first piece is set inside the next

parts.note: a laver is a washing basin
an end is a tip

explanation.surface: Advice to load the washing machine at the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'washer' is a basin, LAVER, not a machine or a ring; END goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavender is a fragrant shrub.

clue.text: Epithet isn't to include a Nereid

indicators.note: include signals letters contained within the words Epithet isn't

explanation.surface: A descriptive name is said to cover a sea nymph.
explanation.definitionFit: Thetis, mother of Achilles, was one of the sea nymphs called Nereids.

indicators.note: two calls for the piece twice

parts.note: a paw is an animal's foot

explanation.surface: A tropical fruit measuring two feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two-foot' looks like a size but doubles PAW.
explanation.definitionFit: The papaya, a tropical fruit, is also called this.

parts.note: discouraged split as dis-couraged, losing courage, with fatally hinting at losing a vital organ

explanation.surface: Someone was utterly disheartened.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means gave up hope; 'fatally' adds losing the organ itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose courage or hope is to be discouraged.

parts.note: L stands for a pound, from libra
per means a, as in so much a head
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A tongue costs a pound per tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' looks like tinned meat but is a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin is a language, and tongue means language.

clue.text: Like some games ? That's an advantage

parts.note: as means like
a set in tennis is a group of games

explanation.surface: Resembling some games is an advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful quality or advantage.

definitions.meaning: a drink of fruit juice, sugar and spirits

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' is a noun for foliage, not a verb for departing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bush bears foliage, and the word is also an old punch-like drink of rum or brandy with fruit.

clue.text: It's designed for a couple of dancers

definitions.text: It's designed for a couple of dancers

parts.words: It's designed for a couple of dancers
parts.note: a dance named after its paces, with couple hinting at the number

explanation.surface: Something made for a pair of dancers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'couple' points to the number in the dance's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballroom dance in duple time danced by partners.

clue.text: None backed to beat this billiards player

indicators.note: backed means the word for none is written backwards

parts.note: nil means none
to drum is to beat

explanation.surface: Nobody has been tipped to defeat this billiards player.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is Walter Lindrum, an Australian billiards champion of the 1930s. The grid's LANDRUM is a misprint.
explanation.definitionFit: An Australian champion widely held the greatest billiards player ever.

clue.text: Poet is said to be sound

indicators.note: said marks words heard rather than spelt

parts.note: noise means sound

explanation.surface: A poet is reputed to be in good health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like healthy but means a noise. Alfred Noyes wrote 'The Highwayman'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Noyes was an English poet.

parts.note: a member of the Royal Army Medical Corps might be a war doctor, WAR plus DR
OBEs are orders of the British Empire

explanation.surface: An army medic commands some furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAMC is the British Army's medical corps; 'Perhaps' shows its man is one example of a wartime doctor. The OBE is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Wardrobes are cupboards for clothes, items of furniture.
